A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GRIFFIN research. Complete text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the methods, equations, figures, tables, and appendices, including v2 Appendices A–F and v3 Appendices A–I.

before.justification: V2 reports original decoding-speed and acceptance-length experiments, including benchmark comparisons and architectural and training ablations in Tables 1–8.

after.justification: V3 retains the original experiments and adds EAGLE-3 comparisons, batched-throughput measurements, latency measurements, and a feature-loss ablation.

M1.justification: Section 4.1 substantively revises the stated training rule: v2 masks and normalizes first-pass losses, whereas v3 uses an unmasked sum. Later masks change from including current-token predictability to depending only on preceding tokens; Equation 4 also restricts inputs to positions before t. These changes affect supervision and causal inputs. TGF/TEH remain unchanged; reruns of retained experiments are not established.

E1.justification: Both versions train on ShareGPT and evaluate conversation, code generation, and mathematical reasoning using MT-Bench, HumanEval, and GSM8K. The added studies reuse existing datasets and tasks. UltraChat-200K is explicitly excluded from the new EAGLE-3 training.

E2.justification: V3 adds EAGLE-3 as an evaluated comparator for LLaMA3-8B across all three benchmarks at temperatures 0 and 1 in Table 1, repeated in Table 10. Existing comparator rows are retained.

E3.justification: The main evaluation settings are retained. Appendix G adds a targeted vLLM throughput protocol using batch sizes 2, 4, 8, and 16, temperature 0, and sequential speculation capped at two tokens, referenced against vanilla vLLM. Appendices D/I specify ShareGPT-only training for the added EAGLE-3 comparison.

E4.justification: New Appendices G–I investigate batch-size sensitivity, decompose decoding latency using measurements, and ablate feature-level supervision. These substantially extend the analysis beyond v2's architectural and training-hyperparameter ablations, which remain unchanged in Tables 2–8.

E5.justification: V3's new checklist item 7 states that inference workloads are run multiple times and argues their variance is minimal. V2 lacks this repetition disclosure. V3 still supplies no run counts, seeds, quantified uncertainty, or significance tests; the statement does not establish an increase in runs.

E6.justification: V3 adds EAGLE-3 and feature-loss-ablation scores, batched-throughput results, and measured forward-pass latencies. Table 9 reports GRIFFIN speedups of 1.52x at batch size 2 and 1.25x at 16 over vanilla vLLM. Table 1 also corrects LLaMA3-8B's temperature-1 mean acceptance length from 5.20 to 5.02 without changing its component values. Tables 2–8 retain their results.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 revises the formal alignment-mask definition and causal indexing. Appendix H newly derives an approximate speedup expression from target latency, draft latency, rollout depth, and acceptance length. These are bounded mathematical revisions and additions; no theorem or proof development is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same token-misalignment novelty claim, two-component contribution, and headline improvements exceeding 8% in acceptance length and 7% in speedup. The new experiments provide additional support without redefining these central claims.

C2.justification: V3 adds explanations for declining batched speedups, the gap between acceptance length and realized speedup, and the benefits of feature supervision. It qualifies the vLLM results because sequential speculation differs from native tree decoding, limits the EAGLE-3 comparison to matched ShareGPT training, and discusses possible transfer of GRIFFIN components.

D1.justification: Appendix C.1 newly specifies token/feature loss weights of 1/0.1. V3 also documents EAGLE-3 training costs and data restrictions, plus vLLM integration details. Existing optimizer settings, hardware, budgets, and draft sizes remain. The abstract changes release wording from completed to planned, conflicting with the new checklist's availability statements; actual access cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: The 35 bibliography entries and Section 2 are retained. Appendix I adds substantive positioning against EAGLE-3's removal of feature supervision and proposes applying GRIFFIN's alignment techniques to EAGLE-3-style models, despite adding no corresponding bibliography entry.

P1.justification: V3 locally rewrites Section 4.1 around predictability and alignment, adds acknowledgments and a NeurIPS checklist, expands implementation documentation, and adds Appendices G–I. Most existing prose and the main section ordering remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains an EAGLE-3 row, and Tables 9–10 add new displays. Figures 1–3 retain their graphics; Figure 3 moves from page 5 to page 6 and gains a clarifying caption. Table placement, spacing, and pagination change without a broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: V3 improves implementability through the revised masking specification and explicit loss weights, corrects a reported average, and adds useful feature-loss, baseline, and throughput checks. The gains are limited by the restricted EAGLE-3 training comparison and unquantified uncertainty. Conflicting code-release statements introduce a small reproducibility-documentation drawback, but the added clarification and evidence support a modest net improvement.
